title: Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias and facial pain

steps.tx: **Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias** are strictly unilateral primary headaches with **ipsilateral cranial autonomic signs** and **restlessness or agitation**. The group is **cluster headache**, **paroxysmal hemicrania**, **SUNCT and SUNA**, and **hemicrania continua**. Attacks range from seconds in SUNCT to 3 hours in cluster, with frequency from once daily to dozens per hour.
steps.say: Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias are strictly unilateral primary headaches with ipsilateral cranial autonomic signs and restlessness or agitation. The group is cluster headache, paroxysmal hemicrania, SUNCT and SUNA, and hemicrania continua. Attacks are brief in SUNCT and are prolonged to three hours in cluster, with frequency ranging from once daily to dozens per hour.

steps.tx: Most TACs are **primary** with **male predominance** in cluster and **female predominance** in paroxysmal hemicrania. **Alcohol and vasodilators** trigger cluster bouts, while stress and neck movement do not. **Secondary mimics** are **pituitary adenoma**, **cavernous sinus lesion**, and **posterior fossa arteriovenous malformation**. Any atypical age, abnormal examination, or poor treatment response is followed by imaging.

points: Clocklike bouts with full autonomic storm

steps.tx: Attacks begin with **posterior hypothalamic activation**, visible on functional imaging during bouts. The **trigeminal autonomic reflex** then produces pain through the **ophthalmic division** and parasympathetic outflow through the **sphenopalatine ganglion**. Release of **calcitonin gene related peptide** and **vasoactive intestinal peptide** produces vasodilatation, lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, and eyelid oedema on the painful side.

steps.tx: Cluster headache causes **excruciating unilateral orbital or temporal pain** lasting **15 minutes to 3 hours**, occurring **1 to 8 times daily** in bouts of weeks. Pain strikes at night, peaks within minutes, and forces pacing or rocking. **Ipsilateral lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, ptosis, and miosis** accompany every typical attack. A **partial Horner syndrome** may persist between bouts.
steps.say: Cluster headache causes excruciating unilateral orbital or temporal pain lasting fifteen minutes to three hours, occurring one to eight times daily in bouts of weeks. Pain strikes at night, peaks within minutes, and forces pacing or rocking. Ipsilateral lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, ptosis, and miosis is present in every typical attack. A partial Horner syndrome may persist between bouts.

steps.tx: Paroxysmal hemicrania gives **brief attacks many times daily**, always aborted by **indomethacin**. **SUNCT and SUNA** give **seconds-long stabs dozens of times daily** with prominent tearing and red eye. **Hemicrania continua** is a **continuous unilateral ache** with superimposed spikes, also indomethacin responsive. **Migraine** lasts longer with nausea and photophobia, while **trigeminal neuralgia** gives electric shocks without autonomic storm.

SUNCT and SUNA cause seconds-long stabs dozens of times daily with prominent tearing and red eye. Hemicrania continua is a continuous unilateral ache with superimposed spikes and is also indomethacin responsive. Migraine lasts longer with nausea and photophobia, while trigeminal neuralgia gives electric shocks without autonomic storm.

left.title: Short TACs
points: Paroxysmal hemicrania: brief, many per day
SUNCT and SUNA: seconds, dozens per day

right.title: Lookalikes
points: Trigeminal neuralgia: electric shocks on touch
Dental pain: local tenderness, no autonomic signs

steps.tx: The first test for any suspected TAC is **contrast MRI of the brain** with dedicated **pituitary and cavernous sinus views**. The gold standard workup is **MR angiography and venography** to exclude dissection, fistula, and venous thrombosis. **SUNCT** needs close **posterior fossa** scrutiny for vascular loops and demyelination. Normal imaging with a typical phenotype confirms a **primary TAC** and treatment response seals the diagnosis.

steps.tx: Acute cluster attacks abort with **high flow oxygen** or **subcutaneous sumatriptan**. **Verapamil in divided doses** is first line prevention with ECG monitoring for block. **Paroxysmal hemicrania and hemicrania continua** are aborted by **indomethacin daily**. Short courses of **corticosteroid** or **greater occipital nerve block** bridge into prevention.

Paroxysmal hemicrania and hemicrania continua are aborted by indomethacin daily. Short courses of corticosteroid or greater occipital nerve block are used to bridge into prevention.

steps.tx: Episodic cluster uses **lithium or topiramate** as targeted prevention when verapamil alone is not enough, while chronic cluster uses **occipital nerve stimulation** or **sphenopalatine ganglion stimulation** in refractory cases. **Short corticosteroid courses** and **greater occipital nerve block** give transitional control. **Trigeminal neuralgia** options differ and include **microvascular decompression** for classic vascular conflict.

nodes.label: Add lithium or topiramate if bouts persist
Chronic refractory: nerve or ganglion stimulation

steps.tx: About **10 to 15 percent** of cluster cases turn **chronic** without remission longer than 3 months. Repeated nocturnal attacks cause **sleep deprivation, depression, and job loss**, with suicide risk higher than in migraine. High dose verapamil can cause **bradycardia, heart block, and ankle oedema**. Most episodic bouts are self-limited, and correct prophylaxis is followed by shorter bouts with restored function within weeks.

left.title: Good prognosis signs
points: Prompt response to oxygen or verapamil

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam:** cluster lasts 15 minutes to 3 hours and 1 to 8 times daily and loves oxygen and sumatriptan. Paroxysmal hemicrania causes brief attacks many times daily and always answers indomethacin. SUNCT gives seconds-long stabs dozens of times daily with red tearing eye. Hemicrania continua is continuous and indomethacin responsive. Verapamil prevents cluster and posterior hypothalamus drives every TAC.
